title: Where it all begins
text: Chinese history starts with a flood and a man with a shovel. Whether Yu was real, his story sets the rule for every ruler after: control the river or lose the throne.

title: The first words
text: The writing you see on Chinese signs today started as questions burned into turtle shells 3,300 years ago.

title: One dynasty falls, an idea is born
text: A rebel king beats a much bigger Shang army in a single morning. The winners need to explain why they deserved to win, so they invent the Mandate of Heaven: rule well, or lose it.

title: The teacher nobody hired
text: A failed politician whose ideas ran China for 2,000 years. Family, duty, education. Still everywhere in East Asia.

title: One China
text: One man forces seven kingdoms into one empire, one script, one road width. He names himself Emperor. The name Qin becomes "China".

title: The Han golden age
text: 400 years of stability. Paper, the Silk Road, and the name Han people still call themselves. Rome is the only comparison.

title: One empire, three pieces
text: A fire on the Yangtze stops China's reunification cold. Three rival kingdoms fight it out for 60 years, and China falls in love with the story for the next 1,800.

title: Briefly, one China again
text: The Three Kingdoms end and Jin reunifies the country. It does not last: succession wars and northern invasions break it apart again within a generation.

title: The conqueror who went native
text: North and south are split for a century and a half. Then a non-Chinese emperor in the north orders his own people to dress, speak and live like the Chinese they rule.

title: Reunited, after 400 years
text: Nearly four centuries of division end almost overnight. The dynasty that does it burns out fast, but it hands the next one a reunified, workable China.

title: Tang: the world comes to China
text: The most cosmopolitan city on Earth is Chang'an. Poets, Persians, Buddhists. And for 15 years, a woman on the throne.

title: The golden age breaks
text: A trusted general turns on the emperor. The rebellion and famine that follow may kill more people, proportionally, than any war in history. Tang never fully recovers.

title: Song: the tech boom
text: Printing, compass, paper money, gunpowder. Song China is centuries ahead of Europe. Then the Mongols arrive.

title: Song loses the north
text: Jurchen armies capture the Song capital and both emperors. The court flees south of the Yangtze and rebuilds — smaller, richer, still inventing.

title: Conquered by the biggest empire ever
text: After 70 years of war, Kublai Khan finishes what his grandfather Genghis started. All of China is ruled by outsiders for the first time.

title: Ming: the fleet that turned back
text: China had the biggest navy on Earth and sent it to Africa. Then burned the records and closed the ports. Europe took the sea instead.

title: The century of humiliation begins
text: Gunboats, unequal treaties, a 20-million-death civil war. The Qing empire falls apart in slow motion. China never forgot.

title: 2,000 years of emperors, gone
text: A bomb accident, a mutiny, and provinces declaring independence one by one. The child emperor abdicates. Nobody quite agrees on what replaces him.

title: The state that exists today
text: After decades of war and revolution, the Communists win and Mao proclaims a new republic from Tiananmen Gate. The Nationalists retreat to Taiwan — a divide that is still unresolved.

title: From famine to superpower
text: Revolution, famine, chaos. Then in 1978 one decision changes everything: let people get rich. 800 million out of poverty. You are here.
